description: Workbench-reviewed closure contrast seed batch. Human-reviewed as a clean contrast set before corpus inclusion.

entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The claim was debunked.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence presents the dispute as closed or refuted and requires an inspectable evidence chain.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Legitimate only if an inspectable evidence chain directly contradicts the exact claim being closed.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: clarify closure/dismissal terms and extract the exact claim
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: not source-driven unless sources are later attached
questions: What exact claim is being closed, dismissed, or refuted?

entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The claim was challenged.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence says the claim is being questioned or contested; this creates challenge pressure, not refutation or falsity.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: A challenge is legitimate as pressure against certainty, but it is not the same as refutation or contradiction.

evidence_burden: Identify what part of the claim is challenged.
Identify the reason or evidence for the challenge.
Check whether the challenge weakens, contradicts, or merely questions the claim.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: treat challenge as challenge pressure only; do not convert it into refutation or falsity
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: not source-driven unless sources are later attached
questions: What part of the claim is challenged, and does the challenge weaken, contradict, or merely question it?

entries.text: The claim was contradicted by the transcript.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The claim was contradicted by the transcript.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence claims an inspectable record conflicts with the claim; contradiction depends on matching definitions, date, and scope.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Transcript evidence is legitimate only when authentic, complete enough for the claim, and mapped to the exact statement.
A record legitimately contradicts a claim only when both cannot be true under the same definitions, date, and scope.

evidence_burden: Map exact quote or absence claim.
Check definitions, timing, and possible reconciliation.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: map the record-to-claim contradiction and check scope before resolution
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: inspect the evidence object directly before support/contradiction movement
questions: What record contradicts the claim, and do the record and claim share the same definitions, date, and scope?

entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The claim lacks evidence.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence withholds support because of an evidence gap; this is not automatically a contradiction or proof of falsity.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Lack of evidence is legitimate as support-withholding pressure; it is not automatically evidence of falsity.

evidence_burden: Identify the claim and expected evidence type.
Check whether evidence was searched for in the right place.
Separate absence of support from contradiction.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: separate evidence gap from falsity or contradiction
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: not source-driven unless sources are later attached
questions: What evidence type is expected, and was the absence of evidence checked in the right place?
Is this only lack of support, or is there positive contradiction?

entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The claim is false.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence asserts falsity and applies closure pressure that requires falsifying evidence.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: A falsity claim is legitimate only when the exact claim is contradicted by evidence or fails under agreed definitions and scope.

evidence_burden: Check definitions, scope, date, and possible weaker interpretation.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: extract exact claim and require falsifying evidence before closure
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: not source-driven unless sources are later attached
questions: What exact evidence falsifies the exact claim?

entries.text: The certified reviewer rated the claim false.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The certified reviewer rated the claim false.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence combines source-status and rating pressure with a falsity claim; the rating must not substitute for the evidence chain.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Certification is legitimate only as metadata about process or status; it does not prove the source conclusion.
A falsity claim is legitimate only when the exact claim is contradicted by evidence or fails under agreed definitions and scope.
A rating is legitimate only as a review output; the rating must be backed by inspectable reasoning and evidence.
Reviewer status is legitimate as role metadata; it does not establish the reviewed claim without reasoning and evidence.

evidence_burden: Check definitions, scope, date, and possible weaker interpretation.
Inspect the evidence and reasoning behind the rating.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: extract exact claim and require falsifying evidence before closure
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat source/status/rating labels as metadata or prior pressure, not truth
questions: What exact evidence falsifies the exact claim?
Who rated the claim, what category was used, and what evidence supports the rating?
Is reviewer/certification status being substituted for claim-level evidence?
